evidence.effect: Accuracy was calculated on a 500-comment stratified manually coded sample per trust against a 75% threshold; initial accuracy fell below threshold in some trusts and recoding brought all to at or above 75%.
evidence.quote: The acceptable threshold for overall accuracy for theme and sentiment for a supervised algorithm using patient feedback was determined at 75%.
evidence.sample_unit: NHS trusts (500-comment stratified manually coded sample per trust for accuracy)

evidence.title: Leveraging Machine Learning and Robotic Process Automation to Identify and Convert Unstructured Colonoscopy Results Into Actionable Data: Proof-of-Concept Study
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of automated process on local scanned reports against chart-review reference standard
evidence.effect: Accuracy 80.7% (557/690, 95% CI 77.8%-83.7%) for identifying presence or absence of valid follow-up date; false negative rate 32.9% (130/395).
evidence.quote: During process validation, the overall automated process achieved an accuracy of 80.7% (557/690, 95% CI 77.8%-83.7%) for correctly identifying the presence or absence of a valid follow-up date and a follow-up date false negative identification rate of 32.9% (130/395, 95% CI 29.4%-36.4%).

evidence.title: Real-World Evaluation of an AI-Assisted Diagnostic Support System for Early Gastric Cancer: Diagnostic Performance, Confidence Stratification, and Determinants of False-Positive Diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Local diagnostic performance of AI against pathology reference standard
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 97.6%, NPV 95.7%, specificity 45.8% on local real-world lesions; false positives remained common.
evidence.quote: The AI system demonstrated a sensitivity of 97.6% and an NPV of 95.7%, with a specificity of 45.8%.

evidence.title: Predictive Utility of the Vedolizumab Clinical Decision Support Tool in a Real-World IBD Cohort: Differential Performance in Crohn's Disease and Ulcerative Colitis
evidence.outcome: Predictive value of CDST risk groups for clinical, endoscopic outcomes and persistence in local real-world cohort
evidence.effect: CDST failed to predict PRO-2 clinical remission; in CD it associated with week-52 CSFR (p=0.04), endoscopic outcomes (p<0.001), persistence (p=0.004); no predictive association in UC.
evidence.quote: In UC, no predictive association was observed for either clinical or endoscopic outcomes nor treatment persistence; however, we observed relatively high remission rates despite CDST-based stratification.

evidence.title: Analytical validation of Smilo.ai: evaluating an AI-driven platform for automated oral health screening and global diagnostic accessibility
evidence.outcome: AI oral condition detection versus dentist reference on local participant photographs; agreement and accuracy
evidence.effect: Overall sensitivity 73.6%, precision 46.0%, accuracy 47.3%, macro Cohen's kappa 0.010; near-zero specificity for decay, tooth wear, discoloration; optimization needed before screening workflow integration.
evidence.quote: Smilo.ai demonstrated an overall sensitivity of 73.6%, precision of 46.0%, accuracy of 47.3%, and a macro-level Cohen's κ of 0.010 relative to dentist assessments.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-guided clavicle fracture detection on plain radiographs: A retrospective diagnostic accuracy study
evidence.outcome: AI performance on local historical radiographs against senior radiologist reference standard
evidence.effect: On local AP radiographs after clinical implementation, AI achieved accuracy 97.31%, sensitivity 95.83%, specificity 98.89%, Cohen kappa 0.95, F1 0.97.
evidence.quote: On AP radiographs, the AI system achieved an accuracy of 97.31%, sensitivity of 95.83%, specificity of 98.89%, Cohen kappa of 0.95, and F1 score of 0.97.

evidence.title: Evaluation of the Efficacy of Artificial Intelligence-Based Screening for Diabetic Retinopathy in a Predominantly Non-White Population
evidence.outcome: Local diagnostic accuracy of FDA-cleared AI DR screening versus reference standard
evidence.effect: The system yielded favorable performance measures in the study population regarding detection accuracy; concluded LumineticsCore was a reliable screening test for DR in the study population.
evidence.quote: The system yielded favorable performance measures in the study population regarding detection accuracy.

evidence.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Only Simulation for Prostate Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Guided Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy
evidence.outcome: Dosimetric agreement of synthetic CT versus planning CT recalculated plans (gamma, PTV D95%)
evidence.effect: Gamma pass 96.80%±1.33% (2%/2 mm local) and 99.98%±0.03% (3%/2 mm global); mean absolute PTV D95% difference 0.06±0.14 Gy.
evidence.quote: Computed γ-indices were 96.80%±1.33% (2% dose deviation, 2 mm dose-to-agreement, 10% threshold, local dose normalization) and 99.98%±0.03% (3%dosedeviation,2mm dose-to-agreement, 10%, global).

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based CTA Software for Real-World Detection of Large-Vessel Occlusion in Acute Ischemic Stroke
evidence.outcome: Local retrospective diagnostic performance of AI LVO detection versus neuroradiologist reference standard
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 84%, specificity 95%, accuracy 93% among 531 CTA examinations; sensitivity 94% for ICA/proximal M1, 87% intermediate, 73% distal M1.
evidence.quote: Overall LVO detection showed a sensitivity of 84%, specificity of 95%, and accuracy of 93%.

evidence.title: Real-world multimetric comparison of four commercial artificial intelligence solutions for intracranial hemorrhage detection
evidence.outcome: Local performance of vendor AI against neuroradiologist reference standard on emergency CT data
evidence.effect: High AUROC (0.96-0.99) and sensitivity (0.85-0.92) locally across four solutions, but precision, specificity and volumetric agreement differed by vendor.
evidence.quote: However, meaningful differences emerged in confirmatory performance and volumetric agreement.

evidence.title: Accuracy of the vedolizumab Clinical Decision Support Tool in Crohn's disease and its association with long-term persistence: A retrospective cohort study
evidence.outcome: Local retrospective accuracy of baseline CDST for clinical remission at weeks 26 and 52
evidence.effect: AUCs for clinical remission were 0.57 (week 26) and 0.64 (week 52); 0.52 (w26) and 0.64 (w52) for corticosteroid-free clinical remission; CDST showed poor diagnostic accuracy.
evidence.quote: AUCs for clinical remission were 0.57 (week 26) and 0.64 (week 52), 0.52 (w26) and 0.64 (w52) for corticosteroid-free clinical remission.

evidence.title: Perception and accuracy of an AI-based contactless wellness screening system in dental setting; a cross-sectional study
evidence.outcome: Agreement of AI contactless vitals with automated and manual reference measurements in local patients
evidence.effect: No significant differences for respiratory rate and oxygen saturation (p>0.05); significant differences for heart rate, SBP, DBP vs automated device (p<0.05); BP limits of agreement ±30 mmHg SBP, ±20 mmHg DBP.
evidence.quote: There were no significant differences between the contactless AI-based device system and automated or manual measurements for respiratory rate and oxygen saturation (p > 0.05).

evidence.title: External Validation of a Web- and Artificial Intelligence-Based HIV/STI Risk Assessment Tool: Performance Evaluation Using Data from Sydney Sexual Health Centre
evidence.outcome: External validation AUC at a new site versus original validation, pretrained models unmodified
evidence.effect: AUCs at SSHC were 0.67 (HIV), 0.70 (syphilis), 0.73 (gonorrhoea), 0.65 (chlamydia), lower than original MSHC validation metrics (0.74-0.87, all p<0.001).
evidence.quote: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values using data from SSHC were 0.67 (95% CI: 0.65–0.68) for HIV, 0.70 (95% CI: 0.69–0.71) for syphilis, 0.73 (95% CI: 0.73–0.74) for gonorrhoea, and 0.65 (95% CI: 0.65–0.66) for chlamydia, which were lower than the original MSHC validation metrics (0.74–0.87, all p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Toward the Autonomous AI Doctor: Quantitative Benchmarking of an Autonomous Agentic AI Versus Board-Certified Clinicians in a Real World Setting
evidence.outcome: Agent performance on historical telehealth encounters against clinician reference
evidence.effect: 81% top-diagnosis concordance and 99.2% treatment plan alignment across 500 consecutive encounters; no clinical hallucinations.
evidence.quote: No clinical hallucinations occurred (e.g., diagnosis or treatment not supported by clinical findings).

evidence.title: Evaluation of the ‘qXR’ Software for the Detection of Pulmonary Nodules and Signs Suggestive of Heart Failure: A Comparative Analysis in a Latin American General Hospital
evidence.outcome: Local agreement of qXR with radiologist reference standard for nodules, cardiomegaly, pleural effusion
evidence.effect: Moderate to substantial concordance for pulmonary nodules and pleural effusion; cardiomegaly more variable with lower agreement across evaluators; overall accuracy acceptable but differed by condition.
evidence.quote: qXR showed higher agreement with radiologist assessments for pulmonary nodules and pleural effusion, achieving moderate to substantial concordance.

evidence.title: Characterizing Documented Psychosocial Stressors in Pediatric Psychiatric Emergencies with an Open-Weight Large Language Model
evidence.outcome: LLM extraction agreement with human raters on local historical intake notes versus human-only reliability
evidence.effect: Human-plus-LLM reliability did not differ significantly from human-only reliability (human κ 0.71–0.94; human-plus-LLM κ 0.70–0.93) across measures.
evidence.quote: In detected-vs-not-detected coding, human-plus-LLM reliability did not differ significantly from human-only reliability across measures (human κ, 0.71–0.94; human-plus-LLM κ, 0.70–0.93).
evidence.sample_unit: intake notes (parseable LLM outputs); 50 notes in human-rater validation

evidence.title: Half of alcohol, drug, and self-harm presentations cannot be identified in coded emergency department data: a diagnostic accuracy study of a large language model
evidence.outcome: LLM performance on local historical data against adjudicated reference standard
evidence.effect: Validated in a week of local attendances (n=2,256) against a conflict-adjudicated reference standard; LLM balanced accuracy 0.942 to 0.982 across the three domains.
evidence.quote: In a validation week, the identification strategies were assessed against a conflict-adjudicated reference standard (n=2,256); the LLM was then applied to n=105,096 annual attendances at the same site.
evidence.sample_unit: emergency department attendances (validation week); 105,096 annual attendances

evidence.title: An LLM-Based Auditing Framework for Targeted Quality Assurance in Cancer Registries
evidence.outcome: LLM disagreement rate against quality-assured registry values on local historical data
evidence.effect: Breast biomarker disagreement ranged from 1.67% (ER) to 9.18% (Ki-67) in 1,852 cases; prostate categorical Gleason variables below 8%, PSA 17.28% in 920 cases.
evidence.quote: For the four breast cancer biomarkers ER, PR, HER2, and Ki-67, the disagreement rate against quality-assured registry values in 1,852 breast cancer cases was lowest for ER at 1.67% and highest for Ki-67 at 9.18%.
evidence.sample_unit: cancer cases (1,852 breast and 920 prostate) used for benchmarking against quality-assured registry values

evidence.title: Applying models of care for total hip and knee arthroplasty: External validation of a published predictive model to identify extended stay risk prior to lower-limb arthroplasty
evidence.outcome: Local validation of published length-of-stay model: discrimination and calibration on local data
evidence.effect: Original model performed poorly in local validation dataset, grossly overestimating length of stay; performance improved after intercept and coefficient adjustment but remained poorly calibrated at low and medium thresholds.
evidence.quote: The original model performed poorly in the validation dataset, grossly overestimating length of stay.

evidence.title: Reducing diagnostic delays in Acute Hepatic Porphyria using electronic health records data and machine learning: a multicenter development and validation study
evidence.outcome: Model performance on local historical data, plus prospective biochemical testing of flagged current patients
evidence.effect: Best referral models F-score 86-91%; diagnosis model F-score 92%. Of 372 flagged patients only 10 recruited for testing, all negative; post hoc, 71% of cases identified earlier, saving 1.2 years.
evidence.quote: However, we were only able to recruit 10 of these patients for biochemical testing, all of whom were negative.
evidence.sample_unit: patients tested for AHP in diagnosis cohort (72 cases, 347 negatives); referral cohort 100,596 patients

evidence.title: A recalibrated prediction model can identify level-1 trauma patients at risk of nosocomial pneumonia
evidence.venue: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
evidence.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of externally developed model on local historical data before and after recalibration
evidence.effect: Original AUC 0.83, mean predicted risk 6.4% vs observed 10.6%, calibration slope 0.63; after full recalibration AUC 0.84, Brier 0.087, calibration improved.
evidence.quote: After full model recalibration, discrimination (AUC 0.84, 95% CI 0.80-0.88) and calibration improved.

evidence.title: Validation in Indonesia of two published scores for mortality prediction after cardiac surgery
evidence.outcome: Local validation of published mortality scores on local historical data against observed in-hospital mortality
evidence.effect: Observed mortality 3.8% vs predicted 2.1% (EuroSCORE II) and 2.4% (ACEF); both poorly calibrated (HL P<0.001); EuroSCORE II AUC 0.774, ACEF AUC 0.638
evidence.quote: In-hospital mortality occurred in 3.8% of the patients and was considerably underestimated both by the EuroSCORE II (2.1%) and ACEF score (2.4%).

evidence.title: Decision-making support systems on extended hospital length of stay: Validation and recalibration of a model for patients with AMI
evidence.outcome: Discrimination of previously developed model on new hospital's historical data against reference outcome
evidence.effect: On new-hospital data the model's AUC fell from 0.828 to 0.702 and recall from 72% to 58%; specificity 75% to 73%, showing worse local performance than original evidence.
evidence.quote: According to the data presented in Table 3 , there is a decrease in the predictive capacity of the VM compared to the results obtained in the model by Magalhães et al. ( 13 ).

evidence.title: External Validation and Comparison of a General Ward Deterioration Index Between Diversely Different Health Systems
evidence.outcome: Model discrimination (AUROC, AUPRC) on local retrospective data from a second hospital
evidence.effect: External hospital AUROC 0.875 (0.851-0.902), AUPRC 0.339 (0.281-0.398) vs 0.870 and 0.298 at the development hospital; performance consistent despite differences.
evidence.quote: PICTURE was able to identify general ward patients at risk of deterioration at both hospitals with consistent performance (AUROC and AUPRC) and compared favorably to existing metrics.

evidence.title: How smart is artificial intelligence in organs delineation? Testing a CE and FDA-approved Deep-Learning tool using multiple expert contours delineated on planning CT images
evidence.outcome: Local external validation of CE/FDA-approved auto-segmentation against expert contours and similarity thresholds
evidence.effect: Unedited MV contours needed adjustment for many OARs; median DSC of adjusted versus MV contours was above 0.8 for all organs except esophagus and glottis in H&N; DSC and MDA thresholds (0.8, 3 mm) used.
evidence.quote: In this study, we evaluated the performance of a DL-based auto-segmentation algorithm on local data, representing an external validation.

evidence.title: Prognostic Value of Machine-Learning-Based PRAISE Score for Ischemic and Bleeding Events in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Heart Association
evidence.outcome: External discrimination and calibration of PRAISE on local ACS PCI cohort versus reference outcomes
evidence.effect: C-statistics for death, MI, and major bleeding were 0.75, 0.61, and 0.62; observed to expected ratios 0.427, 0.260, and 0.106, showing poor calibration and limited discrimination locally.
evidence.quote: The PRAISE score showed limited potential for risk prediction in our validation cohort with acute coronary syndrome.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence for detection of intracranial haemorrhage on head computed tomography scans: diagnostic accuracy in Hong Kong
evidence.venue: Hong Kong medical journal = Xianggang yi xue za zhi
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of ICH detection AI on local institutional historical CT scans vs reference standard
evidence.effect: AUC 0.842 (95% CI 0.791-0.894); at ≥50% threshold 73% sensitivity, 79% specificity, 18.6% PPV, 97.8% NPV, 78.6% accuracy on 1372 local scans (6.1% ICH).
evidence.quote: The model achieved an area under the curve of 0.842 (95% confidence interval=0.791-0.894; P<0.001) for scan-based detection of ICH.

evidence.title: Development and clinical validation of real-time artificial intelligence diagnostic companion for fetal ultrasound examination
evidence.venue: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
evidence.outcome: Retrospective performance of decision support system on clinical cases against confirmed postnatal diagnoses
evidence.effect: Ascertained diagnosis in top-10 list in 93% (full phenotype) and 83% (stepwise) of syndromic cases after adjudication; specificity 94%/96%, sensitivity 99%/84%.
evidence.quote: For syndromic cases, the ascertained diagnosis was within the top-10 list in 93% and 83% of cases using the full-phenotype and stepwise input, respectively, after adjudication.

evidence.title: Clinical evaluation of a deep learning segmentation model including manual adjustments afterwards for locally advanced breast cancer
evidence.venue: Technical innovations & patient support in radiation oncology
evidence.outcome: preclinical local validation endpoint
evidence.effect: Primary time-efficiency endpoint met: time reduction was achieved in 95% of cases including corrections.
evidence.quote: In 95% of the cases, time reduction was achieved while including corrections of the contours when needed.

evidence.title: External validity of an automated delirium prediction model (DEMO) and comparison to the manual VMS-questions: a retrospective cohort study
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of delirium model on external hospital data against chart-review reference
evidence.effect: DEMO predicted 59 of 75 delirium cases (sensitivity 0.79, 95% CI 0.68-0.87; specificity 0.75, 95% CI 0.72-0.77); acceptable performance externally.
evidence.quote: The DEMO predicted 59 out of 75 delirium cases (sensitivity 0.79, 95% CI = 0.68-0.87; specificity 0.75, 95% CI = 0.72-0.77).

evidence.title: Real-world validation of Artificial Intelligence-based Computed Tomography auto-contouring for prostate cancer radiotherapy planning
evidence.venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
evidence.outcome: Local performance of commercial auto-contouring vs manual contours on retrospective local patients (DSC, HD, clinical score)
evidence.effect: Unedited vs manual DSC ranged 0.65 (seminal vesicles) to 0.94 (bladder); median clinical score 4; 2 and 3 of 20 patients not fully satisfactory for the two observers.
evidence.quote: The average values between the two observers of DSC regarding manual vs (fully) automatic contours showed values ranging between 0.65 for seminal vesicles and 0.94 for bladder with significant differences between the two observers for prostate (after editing) and for femoral heads + femurs (this last not clinically relevant).

evidence.title: Validating the Generalizability of Ophthalmic Artificial Intelligence Models on Real-World Clinical Data
evidence.outcome: Glaucoma classification and optic disc segmentation performance of public-trained vs local real-world-data-trained models on local test data
evidence.effect: Public models dropped 8.0% (OD segmentation, to 85.6%) and 18.4% (glaucoma classification, to 76.6%) on RWD; RWD-trained models outperformed public models on RWD by 2.0% and 9.5%.
evidence.quote: RWD models outperformed public models on RWD test sets by 2.0% and 9.5%, respectively, in OD segmentation and glaucoma classification tasks.

evidence.title: Framework for Radiation Oncology Department-wide Evaluation and Implementation of Commercial Artificial Intelligence Autocontouring
evidence.outcome: Commercial AI autocontour agreement with clinically approved contours on local multi-clinic CT data
evidence.effect: High agreement (DSC >0.9) in 27.8%, 32.8%, 34.1% of cases; low agreement (DSC <0.5) in 7.4%, 8.8%, 6.1%; worse in brain and H&N than pelvis and thorax.
evidence.quote: All 3 solutions had low quantitative agreement in 7.4%, 8.8%, and 6.1% of cases (DSC <0.5), performing worse in brain (median DSC = 0.65/0.78/0.75) and H&N (median DSC = 0.76/0.80/0.81).
evidence.sample_unit: patient planning CT scans (859 clinically approved contours)

evidence.title: Evaluating the performance of artificial intelligence software for lung nodule detection on chest radiographs in a retrospective real-world UK population
evidence.outcome: Local retrospective performance against radiologist report and cancer diagnosis reference standards
evidence.effect: Versus radiologist reports: sensitivity 54.5%, specificity 83.2%, PPV 5.5%, NPV 99.0%. Versus cancer diagnosis: sensitivity 60.9%, PPV 5.6%. Considerable underperformance in real-world cohort.
evidence.quote: The software demonstrated considerable underperformance in this real-world patient cohort.

evidence.title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Stratify Normal versus Abnormal Chest X-rays: External Validation of a Deep Learning Algorithm at East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
evidence.outcome: Local retrospective performance of qXR vs radiologist reference standard for normal/abnormal CXR classification
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 99.7% and specificity 67.4% on 1040 local CXRs against two-radiologist ground truth.
evidence.quote: The CAD software had a sensitivity of 99.7% and a specificity of 67.4%.

evidence.title: Evaluating the Reliability of a Remote Acuity Prediction Tool in a Canadian Academic Emergency Department
evidence.outcome: Agreement of algorithm-predicted acuity with nurse eCTAS triage scores on local retrospective ED data
evidence.effect: Exact agreement 48.4%; kappa 0.18 unweighted, 0.25 linear-weighted, 0.36 quadratic-weighted; overtriaged 46.1%, undertriaged 5.5%. Algorithm needs refinement before safe use.
evidence.quote: This machine learning algorithm needs further refinement before being safely implemented for patient use.

evidence.title: External evaluation of the Dynamic Criticality Index: A machine learning model to predict future need for ICU care in hospitalized pediatric patients
evidence.outcome: Multi-institutional model discrimination on local historical data versus reference outcome
evidence.effect: Multi-institutional CI-D models applied to single-site data had AUROC 0.493-0.545 and AUPRC 0.262-0.299, versus AUROC 0.946-0.948 in the multi-institutional dataset; local testing revealed failure.
evidence.quote: Models developed from multi-institutional datasets and intended for application to individual institutions should be assessed locally and may benefit from re-development with site-specific data prior to deployment.

evidence.title: Deep learning performance on MRI prostate gland segmentation: evaluation of two commercially available algorithms compared with an expert radiologist
evidence.outcome: Local validation of commercial prostate segmentation AI against expert radiologist reference on heterogeneous clinical MRI data
evidence.effect: DSC 0.90±0.05 for DLA1 and 0.89±0.04 for DLA2 versus expert reference; no significant difference between algorithms (p=0.8); 123 patients across 7 hospitals, 8 scanners.
evidence.quote: The DSC mean and standard deviation for DLA1 versus the radiologist reference standard (RSexp) was 0.90±0.05 and for DLA2 versus RSexp it was 0.89±0.04.

evidence.title: Preparing for the bedside-optimizing a postpartum depression risk prediction model for clinical implementation in a health system
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Model performance on local post-development AMC data (2019, 2020) against reference outcome
evidence.effect: Model maintained predictive performance on local later-year data (AUC 0.96 in 2019, 0.97 in 2020; sensitivity 0.95, 0.97 at threshold 0.3) though it showed unequal positive prediction rates.
evidence.quote: We found that the original model maintained predictive performance and, while satisfying fairness metrics that prioritized equal error rates, did not create equal positive prediction rates between White and non-White patients.

evidence.title: Validation of a Multivariable Model to Predict Suicide Attempt in a Mental Health Intake Sample
evidence.outcome: Performance of existing suicide attempt model on local historical intake data against reference outcomes
evidence.effect: AUROC 0.77 (95% CI 0.76-0.78); AUPRC 0.02; sensitivity 37.2% at 95% specificity, 18.8% at 99% specificity; top 10% risk captured 48.8% of attempts.
evidence.quote: The model had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.77 (95% CI, 0.76-0.78), an area under the precision-recall curve of 0.02 (95% CI, 0.02-0.02), an expected calibration error of 0.0012 (95% CI, 0.0011-0.0013), and sensitivities of 37.2% (95% CI, 35.5%-38.9%) and 18.8% (95% CI, 17.3%-20.2%) at specificities of 95% and 99%, respectively.

evidence.title: Clinical validation of commercial deep-learning based auto-segmentation models for organs at risk in the head and neck region: a single institution study
evidence.outcome: Agreement of AI auto-contours with expert contours on local historical clinical cases (DSC, mean distance)
evidence.effect: Local validation on 40 cases: mandible DSC 0.90 and 0.91; chiasm DSC 0.28 and 0.30; manual editing likely needed before treatment planning use.
evidence.quote: EC and AC agreement was highest for the mandible (DSC 0.90 ± 0.16) and (DSC 0.91 ± 0.03), and lowest for the chiasm (DSC 0.28 ± 0.14) and (DSC 0.30 ± 0.14) for AccuContour and ProtégéAI respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: head and neck cancer cases (planning CT)

evidence.title: Geometric and dosimetric evaluation for breast and regional nodal auto-segmentation structures
evidence.venue: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
evidence.outcome: Agreement of AI auto-contours with local manual contours, geometric and dosimetric
evidence.effect: Intact-breast AC V95% 97.1% vs MC 98.4% (p=0.02); IMN V90% significantly different; only 62.5% of AC-CWs met ΔV95%<5% when DSC>0.7 vs 94.1% for breasts.
evidence.quote: Before clinical implementation of this auto-segmentation software, an in-depth assessment of agreement with each local facilities MCs is needed.

evidence.title: Metabolic syndrome risk prediction in an Australian sample with first-episode psychosis using the psychosis metabolic risk calculator: A validation study
evidence.venue: Australasian psychiatry : bulletin of Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
evidence.outcome: Model discrimination and calibration on local historical data against reference standard
evidence.effect: C-statistics 0.72 (full) and 0.71 (partial) acceptable, but calibration showed consistent under-prediction of risk; only a very narrow window of clinical usefulness with original model.
evidence.quote: Calibration plots were similar across imputed datasets, showing consistent under-prediction of risk, more extreme for the full model, with predictions becoming more inaccurate at higher predicted risk scores.

evidence.title: Psychosis metabolic risk calculator (PsyMetRiC) in early psychosis: External validation study in Finland
evidence.outcome: Local historical data validation of predictive model against reference standard
evidence.effect: External validation in 278 Finnish patients found acceptable discrimination but miscalibration that required recalibration, showing local validation identified performance problems.
evidence.quote: Calibration plots (Figure 2 , Figure S3 ) show varying degrees of miscalibration for PsyMetRiC across imputed datasets, with predominantly risk underprediction in the full-model, and overprediction in the partial-model.

evidence.title: Addressing the implementation challenge of risk prediction model due to missing risk factors: The submodel approximation approach
evidence.outcome: Local historical validation of submodels
evidence.effect: Of 129 submodels, 80 met eligibility; C-index 0.60-0.63, NPV 0.82-0.92, Brier 0.19-0.19.
evidence.quote: Among 129 submodels, 80 are selected with eligible performance, where C-index ranges from 0.60 to 0.63, NPV ranges from 0.82 to 0.92 and Brier score ranges from 0.19 to 0.19.

evidence.title: Human-in-the-Loop-A Deep Learning Strategy in Combination with a Patient-Specific Gaussian Mixture Model Leads to the Fast Characterization of Volumetric Ground-Glass Opacity and Consolidation in the Computed Tomography Scans of COVID-19 Patients
evidence.outcome: Local validation against predefined Dice criteria
evidence.effect: DSCs exceeded radiologist criteria of DSC ≥0.95/0.8 for lung parenchyma/COVID-19 pneumonia on non-contrast and contrast-enhanced CT scans.
evidence.quote: The performance of the HITL approach in terms of the DSC for non-contrast and contrast-enhanced CT scans yielded values that were superior to the coefficients defined by radiologists (DSC ≥ 0.95/0.8 for normal lung parenchyma/COVID-19 pneumonia).

evidence.title: Performance of Machine Learning Suicide Risk Models in an American Indian Population
evidence.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of existing suicide risk models on local IHS historical data versus reference outcomes
evidence.effect: MHRN AUROC 0.81 (95% CI 0.77-0.85) vs VU 0.68 (0.64-0.72) for 90-day attempts; Spiegelhalter z -89.9 (VU) and 15.5 (MHRN), both P<.001, before recalibration.
evidence.quote: Although the generalization of the MHRN models is notable, all models were poorly calibrated initially, demonstrating the importance of recalibration when applying models to new populations.

evidence.title: External Validation of a Commercial Artificial Intelligence Algorithm on a Diverse Population for Detection of False Negative Breast Cancers
evidence.outcome: AI detection of false negative cancers on local retrospective screening mammograms against 1-year follow-up ground truth
evidence.effect: AI detected 7/13 (54%) false negative cancers in the FFDM cohort and 4/10 (40%) in the DBT cohort missed by the radiologist; median detection 272 and 248 days sooner.
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence was able to detect 7/13 false negative cancers (54%) in the FFDM cohort and 4/10 (40%) in the DBT cohort on the preceding screening mammogram that was interpreted as negative by the radiologist.
evidence.sample_unit: screening mammography examinations (26,694 FFDM and 3,183 DBT)

evidence.title: Multi-Institutional Evaluation and Training of Breast Density Classification AI Algorithm Using ACR Connect and AI-LAB
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
evidence.outcome: Base model performance at each hospital versus holdout test dataset
evidence.effect: The breast density algorithm performed worse at each hospital than on the holdout test dataset, suggesting poor generalizability of the base model.
evidence.quote: The breast density algorithm performed worse at each hospital than on the holdout test dataset, suggesting poor generalizability of the base model.

evidence.title: Validation of a Visual Field Prediction Tool for Glaucoma: A Multicenter Study Involving Patients With Glaucoma in the United Kingdom
evidence.outcome: Predictive accuracy of previously trained model on local real-world UK historical data versus LR and locally trained model
evidence.effect: PKF MD within 2.5 dB at 60 months 75.7%, better than LR models (P<.01) and similar to UK-KF (75.2%, P=.70).
evidence.quote: The predictive accuracy for MD within 2.5 dB of the observed value at 60 months' follow-up for PKF (75.7%) was substantially better than those for the LR models (P < .01 for both) and similar to that for UK-KF (75.2%, P = .70).

evidence.title: External Validation of a Winning Artificial Intelligence Algorithm from the RSNA 2022 Cervical Spine Fracture Detection Challenge
evidence.outcome: Local sensitivity, specificity, F1, AUC of AI on external trauma center CT scans versus competition data
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 86% and specificity 70% in external validation versus 85% and 94% in competition group; sensitivity held but specificity dropped.
evidence.quote: Sensitivity and specificity were 86% and 70% in the external validation group and 85% and 94% in the competition group, respectively.

evidence.title: Temporal validation of machine learning models for pre-eclampsia prediction using routinely collected maternal characteristics: A validation study
evidence.outcome: Temporal validation of existing models on newer local data: discrimination and calibration
evidence.effect: Models 1 and 3 showed stable discrimination versus development; model 2 had significantly lower discrimination. Calibration slopes: model 3 1.02, model 1 1.15, model 2 0.62.
evidence.quote: Compared to the original development models, the temporally validated models 1 and 3 showed stable discrimination performance, whereas model 2 showed significantly lower discrimination performance.

evidence.title: External validation of an AI-based preoperative frailty index using real-world data
evidence.venue: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
evidence.outcome: Association of AI frailty index with postoperative outcomes in an external cohort
evidence.effect: Highest frailty quintile had higher odds of 30-day mortality (OR 4.33, 95% CI 3.91-4.80) and 2.53 times longer hospital stays vs lowest level.
evidence.quote: The developed preoperative frailty index effectively predicts postoperative outcomes in a large and diverse external cohort.

evidence.title: Multicenter Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Surgical Transfusion Risk at 45 US Hospitals
evidence.outcome: External validation of S-PATH on local hospital data versus MSBOS baseline (AUROC, type and screen recommendation rate)
evidence.effect: Median S-PATH AUROC 0.929 vs MSBOS 0.857; S-PATH recommended type and screen for 32.5% vs 51.6% of cases at equal sensitivity (17.9 percentage point median difference)
evidence.quote: The median (IQR) S-PATH AUROC was 0.929 (0.915-0.946), whereas the median (IQR) MSBOS AUROC was 0.857 (0.822-0.884).

evidence.title: Maximizing Lung Cancer Screening in High-Risk Population Leveraging ML-Developed Risk-Prediction Algorithms: Danish Retrospective Validation of LungFlag
evidence.outcome: Model discrimination (AUC) on local historical data in Danish populations versus PLCOm2012
evidence.effect: LungFlag outperformed PLCOm2012 in Population A (AUC: 0.63 vs. 0.60) and showed slightly higher sensitivity in Population B, though differences were minor.
evidence.quote: LungFlag outperformed PLCOm2012 in Population A (AUC: 0.63 vs. 0.60) and showed slightly higher sensitivity in Population B, though differences were minor.

evidence.title: Clinical Characteristics of Gastrointestinal Malignancy and Validation of the IDIOM Model Among Patients With Iron Deficiency Anemia in Thailand
evidence.venue: JGH open : an open access journal of gastroenterology and hepatology
evidence.outcome: Local validation of UK-developed IDIOM model discrimination and calibration on local retrospective data
evidence.effect: AuROC 62.9% (95% CI 56.8-68.9) vs 69.7-77.1% in UK cohorts; calibration slope 0.27, CITL 3.47, indicating poor local calibration and underestimated risk.
evidence.quote: The model demonstrated lower performance in our Thai cohort compared to the original UK cohorts (AuROC 62.9% vs. 69.7%–77.1%).

evidence.title: Development and recalibration of a multivariable type 1 diabetes prediction model for type 1 diabetes across multiple screening studies
evidence.outcome: Calibration (Brier score) of TEDDY-derived model in TrialNet before vs after local recalibration
evidence.effect: Stratified model underestimated risk in TrialNet (Brier 0.40); logistic recalibration improved Brier to 0.16 (p<0.001); ages 8-17: 0.403 to 0.161.
evidence.quote: We observed significantly reduced Brier score values indiciating improved calibration in the recalibrated model compared to either the stratified or original prediction models (Fig. 3 ).
evidence.country: USA, Sweden, Germany, Finland (TEDDY); USA, Canada, Australia (TrialNet)

evidence.title: Automated transformation of unstructured cardiovascular diagnostic reports into structured datasets using sequentially deployed large language models
evidence.outcome: Fine-tuned LLM extraction accuracy on local historical reports against paired structured data and expert annotations
evidence.effect: 98.7% (69,144/70,032 values) on contemporary YNHHS test set; 87.1% against expert annotations in 100 older YNHHS reports
evidence.quote: At YNHHS, HeartDX-LM accurately extracted 69 144 of 70 032 values (98.7%) across 18 fields in the contemporary test set where paired structured data were available.

evidence.title: Performance of the FIND-FH machine learning algorithm for the identification of individuals with suspected familial hypercholesterolemia
evidence.outcome: Local EHR performance of FIND-FH flagged individuals checked by chart review against FH criteria
evidence.effect: Of 340 flagged, 20-32% met modified Simon-Broome or DLCN criteria for at least possible FH; 191 (56%) warranted outreach; 101 (53%) of those had LDL-C <190 mg/dL.
evidence.quote: In the reviewed cohort, 191 (56%) had enough clinical suspicion for FH to warrant outreach.
evidence.sample_unit: individuals in EHR dataset (340 high-probability individuals chart reviewed)

evidence.title: External evaluation of an open-source deep learning model for prostate cancer detection on bi-parametric MRI
evidence.outcome: Model AUC on local retrospective bpMRI data against radiologist and histopathology reference standards
evidence.effect: AUCs of 0.86 (PI-RADS ≥3), 0.91 (PI-RADS ≥4), 0.78 for csPCa; csPCa sensitivity 0.87, specificity 0.53 on 151 patients.
evidence.quote: The model achieved AUCs of 0.86 (95% CI: 0.80-0.92) and 0.91 (95% CI: 0.85-0.96) for predicting PI-RADS ≥ 3 and ≥ 4 exams, respectively, and 0.78 (95% CI: 0.71-0.86) for csPCa.

evidence.title: External validation of deep learning-derived 18F-FDG PET/CT delta biomarkers for loco-regional control in head and neck cancer
evidence.outcome: Performance of externally developed segmentation model on local retrospective PET/CT data for stratifying loco-regional control
evidence.effect: Higher AI-derived ΔPET-GTV stratified loco-regional control (log-rank p = 0.02); 2-year control 94.1% vs 53.6%; clinician found AI volumes acceptable in 78% of cases.
evidence.quote: Patients with higher ΔPET-GTV (i.e. greater tumour shrinkage) had significantly improved loco-regional control (log-rank p = 0.02).

evidence.title: Dual site external validation of artificial intelligence-enabled treatment monitoring for neovascular age-related macular degeneration in England
evidence.outcome: predefined local validation endpoint
evidence.effect: R9 rNPV 1.17 (1.11-1.23) met clinical/statistical superiority; rPPV 1.39 (1.10-1.76).
evidence.quote: The rNPV of 1.17 (1.11-1.23) met predefined criteria for clinical and statistical superiority and accompanied an rPPV of 1.39 (1.10-1.76).

evidence.title: Deep learning for atrioventricular regurgitation diagnosis: an external validation study
evidence.outcome: Model performance on local historical echocardiograms versus cardiologist reference interpretations
evidence.effect: MR AUC 0.98 (95% CI 0.97-0.99), 91% accuracy, 95% sensitivity, 89% specificity; TR AUC 0.96, 84% accuracy, 91% sensitivity, 80% specificity; only 38% of studies received predictions.
evidence.quote: For MR, the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.98 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.97-0.99], with 91% accuracy, 95% sensitivity, and 89% specificity.
evidence.sample_unit: echocardiography studies with model predictions (of 1541 eligible)

evidence.title: Evaluating Deep Learning-Based Commercial Software for Detecting Ischemic Lesions on DWI in Stroke Patients
evidence.outcome: Lesion-level and patient-level sensitivity of commercial AI on local retrospective DWI data versus expert neurologist reference standard
evidence.effect: Lesion-level sensitivity 83.51% (95% CI 79.8-86.8%); patient-level sensitivity 95.31% (95% CI 91.8-97.6%); undetected lesions were smaller, covered fewer slices, and had higher ADC values.
evidence.quote: The software achieved a lesion-level sensitivity of 83.51% (95% CI, 79.8-86.8%) and a patient-level sensitivity of 95.31% (95% CI, 91.8-97.6%).

evidence.title: Domain validation of the CRASH prognostic model for predicting 14-day mortality among patients and traumatic brain injury and intracranial hemorrhage in a Thai emergency department
evidence.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of CRASH model on local retrospective data against observed 14-day mortality
evidence.effect: AuROC 0.92 (Basic) and 0.93 (CT); calibration-in-the-large -0.916 and -1.257, slopes 1.69 and 1.86, showing overestimation of mortality locally.
evidence.quote: However, calibration metrics indicated a systematic overestimation of mortality, suggesting that recalibration of both the intercept and slope is necessary before the model can be implemented in local clinical practice.

evidence.title: Testing the Transportability of the Psychosis Metabolic Risk Calculator in Canada (Quebec): International External Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of UK-developed model on local Quebec historical data
evidence.effect: Full model C=0.74 (95% CI 0.70-0.77), calibration intercept 0.225, slope 1.278; partial model C=0.70, intercept -0.555, slope 0.993.
evidence.quote: Discrimination performance was acceptable (full model C = 0.74, 95% CI, 0.70-0.77; intercept = 0.225; slope = 1.278; partial model C = 0.70, 95% CI, 0.67-0.74; intercept = -0.555; slope = 0.993).

evidence.title: Enabling Drug-Induced Liver Injury Surveillance Through Automated Medication Extraction From Clinical Notes: A Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV Real-World Large Language Models Validation Study
evidence.outcome: LLM performance on representative real-world clinical notes against a reference standard
evidence.effect: Validated on 100 MIMIC-IV discharge summaries against manual gold standard; precision 0.85, recall 1.00, F1 0.92.
evidence.quote: We retrospectively validated an LLM system on 100 randomly sampled Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) discharge summaries.

evidence.title: Validating Radiology Artificial Intelligence Model Performance on Photon-Counting CT Images Using Large Language Models for Ground Truth Extraction
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
evidence.outcome: Feasibility of LLM-extracted ground truth for local validation of AI on local data
evidence.effect: LLM-extracted labels enabled rapid performance assessment across all four diagnostic tasks; no statistically significant differences in performance between PCCT and non-PCCT cohorts.
evidence.quote: LLM-extracted labels enabled rapid performance assessment across all four diagnostic tasks.

evidence.title: External Validation of an Artificial Intelligence Triaging System for Chest X-Rays: A Retrospective Independent Clinical Study
evidence.outcome: Retrospective local validation of AI CXR triage on hospital data versus reference standard
evidence.effect: Weighted ensemble: accuracy 0.854, sensitivity 0.845, specificity 0.861, AUROC 0.927 on 1045 CXRs from a hospital not used for training.
evidence.quote: The weighted ensemble demonstrated the best balance, with an accuracy of 0.854 (95% CI, 0.831-0.874), a sensitivity of 0.845 (0.810-0.875), a specificity of 0.861 (0.830-0.887), and an AUROC of 0.927 (0.911-0.940).

evidence.title: Leveraging large language models to extract smoking history from clinical notes for lung cancer surveillance
evidence.outcome: LLM smoking variable extraction accuracy against manual annotation on local historical notes
evidence.effect: Generative LLMs achieved >96% accuracy across seven smoking variables versus manually annotated Stanford and Sutter notes.
evidence.quote: Generative LLMs achieved superior performance ( > 96% accuracy) across seven smoking variables, with external validation showing robust generalizability (97.5-98.8% accuracy).

evidence.title: Evaluation of artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support systems for caries and periodontal bone loss: An external validation study
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Dental Association (1939)
evidence.outcome: Local retrospective validation of AI caries and bone loss detection against longitudinal ground truth
evidence.effect: Caries: vendor A 78.68% concordance, 80.17% specificity, 96.92% NPV; vendor B 82.43%, 83.76%, 97.36%. Bone loss: vendor A 78.47%, 94.23%, 80.64%; vendor B 73.89%, 93.55%, 75.20%.
evidence.quote: For caries detection, vendor A achieved 78.68% concordance, 80.17% specificity, and 96.92% NPV; vendor B achieved 82.43%, 83.76%, and 97.36%, respectively.

evidence.title: Novel Artificial Intelligence Chest X-ray Diagnostics: A Quality Assessment of Their Agreement with Human Doctors in Clinical Routine
evidence.venue: RoFo : Fortschritte auf dem Gebiete der Rontgenstrahlen und der Nuklearmedizin
evidence.outcome: Agreement of AI chest X-ray systems with radiologist reports on local hospital data
evidence.effect: Human-AZmed Gwet's AC1 0.47-0.72; Human-Gleamer 0.56-0.96; balanced accuracy 0.67-0.85 (AZmed) and 0.71-0.85 (Gleamer); specificity exceeded sensitivity (0.70-0.98 vs 0.45-0.85).
evidence.quote: Radiologists' routine reports were compared against Rayvolve (AZmed) and ChestView (Gleamer, both from Paris, France).

evidence.title: External validation and logistic recalibration of POSSUM and P-POSSUM for predicting postoperative morbidity and mortality after elective hepatic resection
evidence.outcome: Performance of POSSUM/P-POSSUM on local historical data against observed outcomes
evidence.effect: Local validation showed fair discrimination (AUC 0.696-0.755) and miscalibration, with observed event rates higher than median predicted risks, supporting local model updating.
evidence.quote: These observed rates were higher than the median predicted risks for both endpoints, indicating that the models tended to underestimate the event probability in this population.

evidence.title: Retrospective Validation of Clinical Decision Support Tools for Predicting Effectiveness Outcomes in Inflammatory Bowel Disease Patients Treated with Vedolizumab
evidence.outcome: Predictive performance of CDSTs on local retrospective data across remission outcomes at weeks 14, 30, 54
evidence.effect: UC CDST predicted outcomes at week 54 (CREM 33.3% vs 81.8%, p=0.003; CompREM 33.3% vs 86.4%, p<0.001; CSF-CREM 22.2% vs 77.3%, p=0.001). CD CDST showed no significant differences for any outcome.
evidence.quote: For CD patients treated with vedolizumab, the CDST could not predict effectiveness outcomes.
evidence.sample_unit: patients treated with vedolizumab (32 CD, 41 UC)

evidence.title: Real-world evaluation of an automated EEG spike detection software in a tertiary centre compared to a clinical reference standard
evidence.outcome: Local accuracy of IED detection software versus clinical reference standard at default setting
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 81.1% (95% CI 77.6-84.6), specificity 59.9%, PPV 19.9%, NPV 96.3%; high NPV but low PPV with potential over-calling of IEDs.
evidence.quote: At P15's default sensitivity setting, sensitivity for IED detection was 81.1% (95% CI:77.6-84.6), specificity 59.9% (95% CI: 55.5-64.2), positive predictive value 19.9% (95% CI:16.3-23.5) and negative predictive value 96.3% (95% CI:94.6-98.0).

evidence.title: Translating evidence into practice: adapting TrialGPT for real-world clinical trial eligibility screening
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Local performance against expert-adjudicated reference standard
evidence.effect: Against the expert-adjudicated corpus (n = 149): 81.8% sensitivity, 97.8% specificity, PPV 75.0%.
evidence.quote: Against the expert-adjudicated corpus, the system achieved 81.8% sensitivity, 97.8% specificity, and a positive predictive value of 75.0%.
evidence.sample_unit: patient-trial eligibility determinations in expert-adjudicated gold corpus (plus 55 in manual screening comparison)

evidence.title: How threshold customisation affects the performance of a multiclass X-ray AI model for primary care triage: a retrospective study
evidence.outcome: Performance on representative local data against radiologist reference standard
evidence.effect: At 0.15, AI sensitivity 87.3% vs radiologist report 80.7%; specificity 85.0% vs 85.9%.
evidence.quote: At the default recommended threshold, Lunit INSIGHT CXR3 achieved greater sensitivity than the radiologist (87.3% vs 80.7%) with comparable specificity (85.0% vs 85.9%).

evidence.title: Advancing trauma scoring through large language models: automated estimation of injury severity
evidence.outcome: LLM-estimated ISS agreement with human-assigned ISS on local retrospective data
evidence.effect: Weighted Kappa 0.91 (Grok-3), 0.88 (GPT-4), 0.54 (Perplexity); ICC 0.97 GPT-4, 0.92 Grok-3, 0.84 Perplexity; LoA ±5.2, ±7.0, ±9.7.
evidence.quote: Categorical agreement was high in Grok-3 (weighted Kappa = 0.91), and GPT-4 (weighted Kappa = 0.88), but adequate in Perplexity (weighted Keppa = 0.54).

evidence.title: RAPID CTA versus JLK LVO for large vessel occlusion detection: a pragmatic comparison of performance and common pitfalls
evidence.outcome: Local retrospective validation of AI LVO detection against expert reference standard
evidence.effect: In 176 consecutive local patients, both tools achieved AUROC 0.93 against neuroradiologist consensus; misclassification causes reviewed.
evidence.quote: The performance of RAPID CTA and JLK LVO was compared against expert neuroradiologist consensus using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC).

evidence.title: An artificial intelligence prediction model for optimizing patient selection for cardiac imaging for the investigation of suspected coronary artery disease
evidence.outcome: Local model AUROC on geographical validation vs local test set, then after refitting on provincial data
evidence.effect: Local model AUROC fell from 0.807 to 0.714 on rest of province; after updating on provincial data AUROC recovered to 0.794.
evidence.quote: As expected, performance of the local model was lower on the geographical validation cohort than on the local test set (AUROC = 0.714 [95% CI: 0.714, 0.714] vs. 0.807 [95% CI: 0.806, 0.808]).
evidence.sample_unit: elective outpatients undergoing invasive coronary angiography

evidence.title: Clinical-Grade Somatic Variant Interpretation Performance via a Rule-Constrained Large Language Model Framework (Oncology Logic-Informed Variant Evaluator)
evidence.venue: The Journal of molecular diagnostics : JMD
evidence.outcome: Concordance of LLM variant classification with historical laboratory classifications on local clinical cases
evidence.effect: Mean concordance with historical interpretation 97.5% (range 97.4% to 97.6%) across three replicates; 42 variants (2.9%) discordant in at least one replicate.
evidence.quote: Across three replicates, mean concordance with historical interpretation was 97.5% (range, 97.4% to 97.6%).
evidence.sample_unit: variant observations (200 consecutive tumor NGS cases; 1228 unique variants)

evidence.title: External validation of ECG artificial intelligence for emergency and cardiac assessment across a large-scale U.S. healthcare system
evidence.outcome: AUC on U.S. external data versus prespecified non-inferiority benchmarks across ten conditions
evidence.effect: AUCs ranged from 0.883 to 0.949 across ten target conditions; all met non-inferiority criteria relative to prespecified benchmarks.
evidence.quote: Across ten target conditions, AUCs ranged from 0.883 to 0.949; all met non-inferiority criteria.

evidence.title: Evaluating AI diagnostic accuracy in approximal dental caries detection on bitewing radiographs
evidence.outcome: AI caries detection accuracy on local historical radiographs versus expert reference standard
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 73.1%, specificity 94.3%, PPV 64.7%, NPV 96.1%, accuracy 91.6%; detection patterns differed significantly from reference standard (p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Diagnocat™ showed high specificity (94.3%, 95% CI: 92.4%–96.0%) and NPV (96.1%, 95% CI: 94.7%–97.3%), with an overall accuracy of 91.6% (95% CI: 89.7%–93.4%).

evidence.title: Clinical validation and implementation of mSTOP, a machine learning-based, longitudinal prediction model for the early identification of non-small cell lung cancer patients who not benefit from immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of mSTOP on dual-center historical validation cohort
evidence.effect: In 242 metastatic NSCLC patients, mSTOP identified 35.1% of non-responders with PPV 84.8%.
evidence.quote: Diagnostic accuracy was based on a dual-center validation cohort of 242 metastatic NSCLC patients.

evidence.title: Independent validation of the Mosamatic deep learning automated skeletal muscle and adipose tissue segmentation tool in an external Chinese cancer patient cohort
evidence.outcome: Agreement of automated vs manual CT segmentation on local historical data against reference standard
evidence.effect: Median Dice 0.973 muscle, 0.980 VAT, 0.967 SAT; Lin's CCC 0.983-1.000; excellent generalizability without recalibration in Chinese cohort
evidence.quote: The Mosamatic tool displays excellent generalizability to analyse body compositions in Chinese gastric cancer patients and can facilitate cachexia research.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence for histopathological diagnosis and grading of breast cancer in Ethiopia
evidence.outcome: DeepGrade grading performance on local retrospective slides against pathologist reference
evidence.effect: 100% specificity for low-grade tumours, 82.05% sensitivity for high-grade, AUC 0.914, agreement 86.79%, Kappa 0.71 (95% CI 0.51-0.90)
evidence.quote: The DeepGrade model reached a 100% specificity for low-grade tumours and an 82.05% sensitivity for high-grade tumours, with an AUC of 0.914 and an agreement level of 86.79%.

evidence.title: External Validation and Recalibration of a Risk Calculator for Major Bleeding After Diagnostic Kidney Biopsy
evidence.outcome: External validation discrimination and calibration of bleeding risk model against observed major bleeding
evidence.effect: External validation C-statistic 0.78 (95% CI 0.69-0.85), calibration slope 0.72 (0.41-1.02), calibration intercept 0.41 (0.02-0.80); Halifax bleeding rate 4.1% vs 1.9% and 1.8% in London.
evidence.quote: In the external validation cohort, the model showed good performance with an estimated C-statistic of 0.78 (95% CI, 0.69-0.85), calibration slope 0.72 (95% CI, 0.41-1.02), and calibration intercept 0.41 (95% CI, 0.02-0.80).

evidence.title: The Best of Both Worlds: How Combining a Large Language Model and a Rule-Based Algorithm Makes Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infection Surveillance More Efficient
evidence.venue: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
evidence.outcome: LLM sensitivity and specificity for CAUTI classification on local historical cases versus infection preventionist gold standard
evidence.effect: Combined rule-based logic plus CLEAR-LLM achieved sensitivity 90.0% and specificity 93.5% on 919 local flagged cases; after adjudication 93.6% and 98.6%.
evidence.quote: Combining rule-based logic with Clinical Entity Augmented Retrieval (CLEAR) input into an LLM achieved the highest sensitivity (90.0%) and specificity (93.5%).

evidence.title: Clinical validation of an artificial intelligence model for thyroid fine-needle aspiration biopsy indication: comparison with TI-RADS systems and human specialists in a Chilean public hospital
evidence.outcome: AI performance on local retrospective data against cytology reference standard
evidence.effect: On 101 local patients using Bethesda ≥ III as reference, AI sensitivity was 0.88 and specificity 0.41, described as comparable to human specialists.
evidence.quote: In a real-world clinical setting, the AI model demonstrated performance comparable to that of human specialists for recommending FNA in thyroid nodules.

evidence.title: Expert Validation of an Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Trial Matching Solution Using Real-World Data From Patients With Cancer
evidence.outcome: Performance against expert reference standard on real-world EHR data
evidence.effect: At predefined threshold 0.40, sensitivity 78.3%, specificity 98.5%, PPV 92.6%, NPV 94.8% on held-out test set with CRC adjudication.
evidence.quote: At the predefined trial-level decision threshold for eligibility (0.40), the sensitivity was 78.3%, the specificity was 98.5%, the PPV was 92.6%, and the NPV was 94.8%.

evidence.title: External Validation of a Logistic Regression Model to Predict Cesarean Section Risk in Indian Women
evidence.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of existing model in independent external cohort without refitting
evidence.effect: AUC 0.82; Hosmer-Lemeshow χ2 = 4.26, P = 0.3719; accuracy 81.7%, sensitivity 90.0%, specificity 73.3% at 0.50 threshold
evidence.quote: In the external cohort, the model demonstrated good discrimination (AUC: 0.82) and satisfactory calibration (HL χ2 = 4.26, P = 0.3719).

evidence.title: Performance of GPT-based large language models in hepatocellular carcinoma stratification: liver function assessment, BCLC staging, and treatment recommendations
evidence.outcome: GPT accuracy on local retrospective HCC patient data vs expert consensus and tumor board decisions
evidence.effect: Liver function accuracy >85% across versions; BCLC staging 46.2% (GPT-4) to 84.0% (o3); treatment recommendation overall accuracy up to 90.6%.
evidence.quote: BCLC staging accuracy ranged from 46.2% (version 4) to 84.0% (o3), with misclassification of radiological reports as the main error source.

evidence.title: Cross-anatomical evaluation of a deep-learning auto-contouring system: qualitative, geometric, and dosimetric validation
evidence.venue: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
evidence.outcome: Local retrospective validation of auto-contours against manual contours: usability, geometric agreement, dosimetric impact
evidence.effect: 76.1% of auto-contours clinically usable (score ≥3); DSC >0.8 in 54.8%, MDA <2.5 mm in 71.5%, max HD <12.5 mm in 50%; 88.1% of organs within ±5% dose-volume difference.
evidence.quote: Overall, 76.1% of auto-contours were qualitatively judged to be clinically usable (score ≥3).

evidence.title: Deep learning in glaucoma referral: Performance assessment using a real-world setting
evidence.outcome: Local retrospective performance of AI against specialist reference standard for referable glaucoma
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 1.00 (95% CI 0.82-1.00), specificity 0.65 (95% CI 0.53-0.75), PPV 0.41 (95% CI 0.27-0.57); would have prevented 36 (37.5%) referrals with no glaucoma cases missed.
evidence.quote: The model presented high sensitivity (1.00; 95% CI 0.82-1.00), and reasonable specificity (0.65; 95% CI 0.53-0.75) and positive predictive value (0.41; 95% CI 0.27-0.57).

evidence.title: Comprehensive Performance Testing and External Validation of an AI Algorithm to Detect and Segment Brain Metastases
evidence.outcome: AI sensitivity, false positives, and Dice on external datasets versus consensus reference standard
evidence.effect: FDA testing sensitivity 90.0%, DSC 0.86; augmented external cohort sensitivity 81.4%, DSC 0.70; open-access cohort sensitivity 85.2%, DSC 0.78, showing lower performance externally.
evidence.quote: In the augmented and open-access external validation cohort, a sensitivity of 81.4% (95% CI: 73.7%-89.1%) and 85.2% (95% CI: 83.0%-87.4%) with an average number of 0.22 and 1.19 FP lesions and DSCs of 0.70 (95% CI: 0.66-0.73) and 0.78 (95% CI: 0.77-0.78) were calculated, respectively.

evidence.title: External Validation of Two AI Systems for Dentinal Caries Detection: A Retrospective Pilot Clinical Outcomes Study
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity of two AI systems for dentinal caries on local historical radiographs against clinical outcomes
evidence.effect: Vendor A sensitivity 48.5% (95% CI 37.0-60.2), Vendor B 57.5% (95% CI 46.1-68.2), pooled 53.0% (95% CI 44.8-61.1); local validation feasible and revealed modest sensitivity.
evidence.quote: Vendor A achieved a sensitivity of 48.5% (95% CI: 37.0-60.2), Vendor B achieved 57.5% (95% CI: 46.1-68.2), and pooled sensitivity was 53.0% (95% CI: 44.8-61.1).

evidence.title: Postpartum readmission for hypertension: Validating a predictive model with incorporation of neighborhood-level social determinants of health
evidence.outcome: Discrimination of original calculator on local data versus published, and after local recalibration
evidence.effect: Original calculator c-statistic 0.71 (BTH) and 0.61 (PFW) vs 0.80 originally; calibration poor; after refit c-statistics 0.84 and 0.74.
evidence.quote: This performance was lower than the original calculator's published model discrimination (c‐statistic 0.80), and calibration was poor.

evidence.title: Development and evaluation of AI-based clinical decision support system for streamlining breast multidisciplinary team meetings
evidence.outcome: Concordance of CDS recommendations with MDT decisions on local historical cases across iterative cohorts
evidence.effect: Concordance improved from 82% to 100% in benign and from 94% to 100% in malignant cases through stepwise refinement on retrospective patient cohorts.
evidence.quote: Concordance improved from 82% to 100% in benign and from 94% to 100% in malignant cases.

evidence.title: Clinical evaluation of novel deep learning-based auto-segmentation software: Utility and potential pitfalls
evidence.venue: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
evidence.outcome: Auto-segmentation accuracy versus expert manual contours on local clinical cases, typical versus atypical
evidence.effect: Typical thorax DSC 0.856, HD95 6.89 mm; atypical thorax DSC 0.808 (p=0.0457), HD95 12.22 mm (p=0.0002); pelvis atypical HD95 6.16 mm vs 4.11 mm (p=0.0075).
evidence.quote: However, performance declined in atypical cohorts (thorax: mean DSC 0.808, p = 0.0457, mean HD95 12.22 mm, p = 0.0002; male pelvis: mean DSC 0.828, p = 0.1620, mean HD95 6.16 mm, p = 0.0075).
evidence.sample_unit: cases (thoracic and male pelvic radiotherapy planning CT)

evidence.title: Leveraging ECG foundation models in critical care for sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation classification
evidence.outcome: Off-the-shelf vs locally fine-tuned ECG-FM performance on local expert-labelled ICU data
evidence.effect: Off-the-shelf model F1 0.523 (AF) and 0.677 (SR) on Amsterdam UMC Expert; after fine-tuning F1 0.814/0.914 (public only) and 0.830/0.920 (with local weak data).
evidence.quote: Evaluation of publicly released ECG-FM in Experiment 2 on the Amsterdam UMC dataset demonstrated limited generalisation.
evidence.sample_unit: ECG segments (10-second ICU segments from 226 patients, expert-annotated test set)

evidence.title: Automating the Management of Extraspinal Findings in Magnetic Resonance Imaging Spine Studies Using a Privacy-Preserving Large Language Model: Retrospective Validation Study
evidence.outcome: PP-LLM accuracy on local historical MRI reports versus clinician reference standard
evidence.effect: Detected 99.8% (400/401) of ESFs; Gwet kappa 0.959 versus reference standard, comparable to two human readers (0.943, 0.934); 8 downgraded and 4 upgraded C-RADS classifications.
evidence.quote: The PP-LLM demonstrated almost perfect agreement with the reference standard (Gwet κ=0.959, 95% CI 0.937-0.981), comparable to two human readers (reader 1: κ=0.943; reader 2: κ=0.934), with no statistically significant difference in C-RADS classification accuracy.

evidence.title: Importance of model governance in clinical AI models: case study on the relevance of data drift detection
evidence.outcome: Temporal validation of model performance on later historical data
evidence.effect: XGBoost achieved AUC 0.82 and Brier score 0.158 in temporal validation (Jan 2020 to Oct 2022) after training on data through January 2020.
evidence.quote: The XGBoost model achieved an AUC of 0.82 and a Brier score of 0.158 during temporal validation from January 2020 to October 2022.

evidence.title: Testing Transferability of a Mortality Risk Model for Interhospital Transfer Using Real-World Electronic Health Records: External Validation and Model Enhancement
evidence.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of published model on local historical data versus reference standard
evidence.effect: SafeNET applied unmodified locally gave AUC-ROC 0.87, F1 0.73, Brier 0.055, close to published performance despite extensive missingness.
evidence.quote: These findings indicate that SafeNET maintained predictive performance for in-hospital mortality comparable to its originally reported results, despite substantial dataset shift and extensive missingness in our real-world EHR data.

evidence.title: An intelligent OCR-LLM prescription review system for inpatient narcotic and psychotropic drugs: Development and retrospective validation
evidence.outcome: System accuracy, sensitivity, specificity versus pharmacist review on local retrospective prescriptions
evidence.effect: 144 TP, 16 FP, 334 TN, 6 FN; accuracy 95.6%, sensitivity 96.0%, specificity 95.4%, PPV 90.0%, NPV 98.2%, F1 0.929, kappa 0.897.
evidence.quote: In the retrospective validation, compared with pharmacists' manual review, the system identified 144 true positives, 16 false positives, 334 true negatives, and 6 false negatives.

evidence.title: Distillation of a Locally Deployable 8B Language Model for Lung Histology Abstraction: A 33-Report Proof-of-Concept Study
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of local LLM on local hospital reports vs expert audit
evidence.effect: Distilled Med42-8B achieved 90.91% accuracy, macro F1 0.92 (kappa 0.86) on 33 audited TMUH reports, versus 78.79% accuracy and F1 0.79 for Llama-3-8B.
evidence.quote: Within the audited 33-case clinical subset, the distilled domain-specific Med42-8B model demonstrated a diagnostic accuracy of 90.91% and a macro F1-score of 0.92 (substantial agreement with experts, κ = 0.86), significantly outperforming the general-purpose Llama-3-8B student model (accuracy: 78.79%, macro F1-score: 0.79).

evidence.title: Locally deployed large language model for real-world lecanemab eligibility pre-screening.
evidence.outcome: Accuracy against expert consensus on independent hold-out set of local memory clinic reports
evidence.effect: Optimized on development set (n = 97) and evaluated on independent hold-out set (n = 99); 94% accuracy, kappa 0.90 against expert consensus.
evidence.quote: In a two-stage design, LLM-based extraction prompts, a deterministic rule-based extractor, and a shared downstream rule-based classifier were optimized on a development set (n = 97) and evaluated on an independent hold-out set (n = 99), with expert consensus as ground truth.

evidence.title: Enhancing Early Detection of Cognitive Decline in the Elderly: A Comparative Study Utilizing Large Language Models in Clinical Notes
evidence.outcome: Model performance on local EHR data against annotated reference standard
evidence.effect: Models trained on local EHR data showed diverse error profiles; ensemble improved precision from 70%-79% to above 90%; only 2 of 63 errors (3.2%) were mutual across models.
evidence.quote: LLMs and traditional machine learning models trained using local EHR data exhibited diverse error profiles.

evidence.title: Preoperative risk prediction models for acute kidney injury after noncardiac surgery: an independent external validation cohort study
evidence.outcome: Discrimination, calibration and net benefit of nine published AKI models on a local retrospective cohort
evidence.effect: Three models had fair discrimination (AUROC 0.71-0.75); other models had poor or failed discrimination. All models exhibited some miscalibration.
evidence.quote: Three models demonstrated fair discrimination (AUROC between 0.71 and 0.75); other models had poor or failed discrimination.

evidence.title: Adaptation of risk prediction equations for cardiovascular outcomes among patients with type 2 diabetes in real-world settings: a cross-institutional study using common data model approach
evidence.outcome: External validation of risk equations on local historical EHR data against outcomes with predefined acceptance criteria
evidence.effect: UKPDS-OM2 had unsatisfactory discrimination (AUROC 0.57-0.65); CHIME acceptable (0.71-0.79) but calibration unsatisfactory (GND p<0.001 for most), so local validation revealed the need for adaptation.
evidence.quote: Overall, all the CVD risk equations from UKPDS-OM2 and the stroke risk equation from RECODe demonstrated unsatisfactory discrimination (AUROC < 0.7) for Taiwanese type 2 diabetes populations, and all the CVD risk equations from the CHIME model yielded acceptable discrimination (AUROC ≥ 0.7).

evidence.title: Why implementing machine learning algorithms in the clinic is not a plug-and-play solution: a simulation study of a machine learning algorithm for acute leukaemia subtype diagnosis
evidence.outcome: AI-PAL discrimination on local historical hospital data versus published validation results
evidence.effect: AUROC dropped to 0.67 (95% CI 0.61-0.73) for ALL and 0.71 (0.65-0.76) for AML, below the worst original validation cohort (0.78, 0.80).
evidence.quote: Evaluation of the unmodified AI-PAL algorithm at UME showed a lower performance compared to the four cohorts from the AI-PAL external validation ( Fig. 3 , Supplementary Table S1 ).

evidence.title: Evaluation and tuning of a commercial automated planning system for prostate radiotherapy
evidence.venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
evidence.outcome: Local historical plan quality of automated plans versus clinical plans, and effect of tuning
evidence.effect: Baseline model had inferior rectum sparing (mean rectum V40Gy 0.04 higher); after two tuning iterations, differences were small (mean difference -0.01 rectum V40Gy, -0.03 PTV48 D98%).
evidence.quote: The Bland–Altman plots, supplementary Material S4, showed little difference between the original and automated plans for the third iteration.

evidence.title: Comparative Performance of Large Language Models in Ophthalmology Referral Triage
evidence.outcome: LLM classification accuracy on real local historical referrals against ophthalmologist reference labels
evidence.effect: Baseline mean accuracy 68.7% (2,631/3,831), improving to 73.4% after exposure; model accuracy ranged 65.6%-71.5% at baseline, with weakness in rare categories.
evidence.quote: In the first phase, the overall mean classification accuracy across all models was 68.7% (2,631/3,831).

evidence.title: Clinical evaluation and regression test of a commercial deep-learning auto-segmentation model
evidence.venue: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
evidence.outcome: Local performance of DLS versus clinical reference contours, with decision on commissioning by site
evidence.effect: Abdomen commissioned (DSC 0.95 ± 0.014); breast model not recommended for clinical use (DSC 0.66 ± 0.15, HD95 22.2 ± 9.6 mm) against local reference.
evidence.quote: Breast segmentation results showed low performance (DSC 0.66 ± 0.15, MSD 4.8 ± 1.93 mm, and HD95 22.2 ± 9.6 mm) compared to clinical reference, so the breast structure models are not recommended for clinical use.

evidence.title: An ambiguity taxonomy for evaluating large language model performance on clinical registry abstraction: a multi-site prospective study
evidence.outcome: LLM answer accuracy against abstractor consensus on local EMR data for registry questions
evidence.effect: 87% of LLM answers exactly matched consensus, 2% partially, 9% did not; mean question-level accuracy 91.5% (SD 13.4%); human inter-rater agreement about 98%.
evidence.quote: In validation, human inter-rater agreement was approximately 98\% while 87\% of LLM answers exactly matched consensus, 2\% partially, and 9\% did not.

evidence.title: Image-only ultrasound AI for dating-independent delivery-date prediction externally validated in four Chilean hospitals
evidence.outcome: Delivery-date prediction error (MAE) in external validation at four Chilean public hospitals
evidence.effect: MAE 6.9 days (95% CI 6.7-7.0) across 3,788 studies; 6.4 days in pregnancies lacking reliable first-trimester dating vs 13.2 days for the due date.
evidence.quote: Across 3,788 singleton studies from 2,550 pregnancies at four Chilean public hospitals, the AI predicted the delivery date with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 6.9 days (95% confidence interval [CI] 6.7–7.0).

evidence.title: Diagnostic accuracy of a DenseNet-121 deep learning algorithm for chest radiograph triage in health assessment applicants: a prospective shadow-mode validation study in Nepal
evidence.outcome: Local diagnostic accuracy versus radiologist reference standard in prospective shadow-mode
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 95.12%, specificity 77.2%, AUROC 0.9583, NPV 99.67%, PPV 17.89%; calibration failed despite preserved discrimination.
evidence.quote: The DenseNet-121 algorithm demonstrated high sensitivity and excellent discrimination for chest radiograph triage in a Nepali health-assessment population, supporting its potential as a rule-out tool (NPV 99.67%).

evidence.title: Real-world post-deployment performance of a novel machine learning-based digital health technology for skin lesion assessment and suggestions for post-market surveillance
evidence.outcome: Real-world sensitivity and specificity versus pre-market performance and sensitivity targets
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 95.0-100.0% for melanoma and 96.0-100.0% for malignancy; benign specificity 40.7-49.4% (vA) and 70.1-73.4% (vB); 15.0-31.0% of cases eligible for discharge.
evidence.quote: We show DERM performance in-line with sensitivity targets and pre-marketing authorisation research, and it reduced the caseload for hospital specialists in two pathways.

evidence.title: Clinical Implementation of an Artificial Intelligence Algorithm for Magnetic Resonance-Derived Measurement of Total Kidney Volume
evidence.outcome: Whether validated AI performance was preserved when implemented in local clinical practice
evidence.effect: Algorithm showed high agreement and was noninferior to interobserver variability; performance preserved when implementation environment matched development conditions.
evidence.quote: Performance of an AI algorithm in real-life clinical practice can be preserved if there is careful development and validation and if the implementation environment closely matches the development conditions.

evidence.title: Diagnostic performance with and without artificial intelligence assistance in real-world screening mammography
evidence.outcome: Local AI missed-cancer rate compared with previously published same-platform performance
evidence.effect: The local AI-CAD missed-cancer rate was 34% (10/29), compared with 11–19.4% in previously published studies using the same platform.
evidence.quote: However, the false-negative rate of AI-CAD, also known as the missed cancer rate, was 34% (10/29), which was higher than previously published studies using the same platform at 11–19.4% [12] , [28] .

evidence.title: Prediction of cardiovascular risk factors from retinal fundus photographs: Validation of a deep learning algorithm in a prospective non-interventional study in Kenya
evidence.outcome: Model performance on local Kenyan data versus development data
evidence.effect: MAE comparable or slightly greater; DM AUROC 0.762 (0.818 in UK Biobank); hypertension AUROC 0.765 (0.738 in UK Biobank).
evidence.quote: The model trained to identify DM had an area under the receiver operating curve of 0.762 (0.818 in the UK Biobank) and the hypertension model had an area under the receiver operating curve of 0.765 (0.738 in the UK Biobank).

evidence.title: Comparison of 21 artificial intelligence algorithms in automated diabetic retinopathy screening using handheld fundus camera
evidence.outcome: Agreement of 21 AI algorithms with ophthalmologists for referable DR on local prospective data
evidence.effect: Mean agreement 79.4% (range 49.4% to 92.3%); mean sensitivity 77.5% (95% CI 69.1-85.8), specificity 80.6% (95% CI 72.1-89.2).
evidence.quote: The performance of the AI algorithms varied considerably emphasizing the need for external validation of screening algorithms in real-world settings before their clinical application.

evidence.title: Deep Learning to Detect Intracranial Hemorrhage in a National Teleradiology Program and the Impact on Interpretation Time
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic performance of AI for ICH in a real-world teleradiology practice
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 75.6%, specificity 92.1%, accuracy 91.7%, prevalence 2.70%, PPV 21.1% across 61,704 exams.
evidence.quote: The AI solution had a sensitivity of 75.6%, specificity of 92.1%, accuracy of 91.7%, prevalence of 2.70%, and positive predictive value of 21.1%.

evidence.title: Comparison of 1-year mortality predictions from vendor-supplied versus academic model for cancer patients
evidence.outcome: Local AUC of vendor EOLCI for 1-year mortality versus vendor-stated AUC
evidence.effect: EOLCI AUC 0.73 (95% CI 0.70-0.76) vs vendor-stated 0.86; academic model AUC 0.82 (0.80-0.85). PPV 0.38 vs 0.65.
evidence.quote: The EOLCI's discrimination performance was lower than the vendor-stated value (AUC of 0.86) and the academic model's performance.

evidence.title: Review and reflections on live AI mammographic screen reading in a large UK NHS breast screening unit
evidence.outcome: AI performance on local screening population versus human readers
evidence.effect: Eight cancers (8.79% of total cancers detected) recalled by human readers were not detected by AI; no additional cancers detected by AI.
evidence.quote: Performance of AI was inferior to human readers in our unit.
